newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up in thin trading but flax lower.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up in thin trading but flax lower.

text.p: WCE canola futures settled firmer in the front months as farmer hedge selling capped late afternoon gains, traders said.
The early strength in canola was in line with the early runup in the CBOT soy complex, one trader said
Flax futures ended weaker amid light trading.
"It was more of a lack of buying than anything. Exporters were also backing off," the trader said of activity in flax. Volume in both canola and flax was thin, he added.
July canola inched up C$0.30 to C$425.50 a tonne and July flax dropped C$4.40 at C$334.80.
Lower Chicago corn futures prompted some liquidation in western barley futures, another trader said.

Commission house sell stops were touched off and prompted a July session low in western barley of C$139.00. July western barley lost C$1.50 at C$139.50 a tonne and July feed wheat fell C$2.40 at C$165.20.
Most of the sell stops were in the front months of feed wheat which took the brunt of the pressure, the second trader said.
There were no trades, just commercial offerings in oats and feed peas, he said.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
